_comment: What the fabricator builds. .github/workflows/fabricator.yml reads this and
builds every order in it, and nothing else: it does not look for work.
Each order names the image it publishes (ghcr.io/<repository>-<name>) and
the directory holding its Dockerfile, which is also the build context.
Completeness is checked by a guard, not by the fabricator:
tests/go/repo/fabricator_test.go walks the repository and fails on a
Dockerfile with no order here, and on an order whose Dockerfile is gone.
So adding an image is adding its order, on the same pull request.
An order may also say how to make a release of what it builds, under
release: the production overlay and the module it builds on, which are
staged with the new image digest and published as
ghcr.io/<repository>-<name>-release:<version>; and how the version is read -
the environment the image needs in order to start, and the sed pattern that
captures the version from what it prints. The version is what the built
thing says it is, plus a counter for rebuilds of the same version: 1.0.15-1,
then 1.0.15-2. Nothing here is the fabricator's knowledge; it follows the order.
